narrative:
The model predicted an 84% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is so high, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your third-year class ranking had the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward failure. While the average student who is accepted sits around the 5th or 6th decile in their third year, you placed in the bottom decile. This large gap signaled to the model a high risk of struggling with the bar exam.

Your LSAT score was the second most important factor and also pulled the prediction toward failure. At 20, your score sits far below the 37-point average of accepted students, indicating the model saw this as another clear warning sign.

Your first-year class ranking worked in the opposite direction, modestly encouraging the model to predict success. Placing in the 5th decile was only slightly below the 6th-decile average of accepted students, so this offered a small positive note, but it was not nearly enough to offset the other two factors.

Given these results, you should focus on improving your academic performance and retaking the LSAT. Raising both your class standing and test score would substantially increase your chances on a future application. Consider working with a tutor or academic support program before reapplying.
